notes: Hand-composed by Claude Code under the MVA-only keywordScope rule. Drops the prior universe's premises-liability, medical-negligence, workplace-injury, and standalone catastrophic/wrongful-death themes — all out of scope per Roden's transport-only focus. Roden already has very deep in-scope practice-area coverage (107 of 348 PA slugs are transport-related), so true gaps are mostly sub-type modifiers (rollover MVC, lane-change, drowsy/texting, jackknife, under-ride, tire-blowout) and UM/UIM dedicated pages. The tracking set narrows previously generic ranker terms (e.g. 'brain injury lawyer' → 'brain injury car accident lawyer', 'wrongful death lawyer' → 'wrongful death car accident lawyer') so SoLV pressure stays inside scope. Top 3 strategic moves: (1) build dedicated underinsured-motorist + lane-change MVC sub-type pages, (2) expand commercial-truck sub-types (jackknife, under-ride, tire-blowout) where Roden already owns 18-wheeler/cement/port pillars, (3) deepen rideshare-passenger vs rideshare-driver split (insurance-coverage gap most firms miss).

themes.label: Car and passenger-vehicle collisions
themes.rationale: Roden's highest-volume case type. Anchors the MVA universe across all 6 offices (Savannah, Darien, Charleston, N. Charleston, Columbia, Myrtle Beach). Interstate corridors I-95, I-26, I-77, I-20, US-17.

themes.label: Commercial trucks and freight
themes.rationale: Highest-value case category. Port of Savannah, Port of Charleston, and the I-95 freight corridor drive volume. Roden already owns 18-wheeler, port-freight, and fatigued-trucker pages; gap is sub-type modifiers competitor firms rank for.

themes.label: Motorcycles and mopeds
themes.rationale: Coastal touring routes (US-17, Highway 80, Cherry Grove) drive year-round motorcycle volume. Distinct biker-bias defenses + helmet-statute issues per state. Roden owns intersection-, hit-and-run-, drunk-driver-, and head-on-motorcycle sub-types — gap is lane-splitting and product-defect angles.
long_tail: hit and run motorcycle accident lawyer

themes.label: Rideshare, taxi, and livery
themes.rationale: Charleston peninsula, Myrtle Beach nightlife, downtown Columbia, and Savannah River St all drive heavy rideshare volume. Distinct insurance-tier coverage (off-app vs Period 1 vs Period 2/3) is the angle most local firms miss.
long_tail: uber eats delivery driver accident lawyer
gaps: uber eats delivery driver accident lawyer

themes.label: Buses
themes.rationale: Public transit (CARTA Charleston, COMET Columbia), school buses, and tourist charter buses (downtown Charleston, Savannah ghost tours, Myrtle Beach charters) all generate distinct claims. Government-defendant Tort Claims Act triggers in SC make timely notice critical.

themes.label: Pedestrians
themes.rationale: Tourist-walking density — Charleston peninsula, Tybee, Folly, Murrells Inlet boardwalk, Myrtle Beach Boulevard — drives year-round pedestrian-struck volume. Roden owns school-zone, intersection, hit-and-run, drunk-driver, and distracted-driver pedestrian sub-types — gap is parking-lot and crosswalk-specific keywords.
long_tail: hit and run pedestrian accident lawyer

themes.label: Bicycles and micromobility (e-bike, e-scooter)
themes.rationale: Beach-town and downtown bicycle, e-bike, and e-scooter rentals (Charleston, Savannah, Myrtle Beach) and the rise of e-scooter share programs create rapidly growing micromobility claims. Roden owns intersection, road-hazard, drunk-driver, and distracted-driver sub-types in bicycle + e-scooter — gap is dooring and bike-lane-specific keywords.

themes.label: ATV, side-by-side, UTV, and golf carts
themes.rationale: Coastal Lowcountry hunting/farm ATV use + Surfside/Pawleys/Sea Pines golf-cart-permissive streets generate distinct off-road and low-speed-vehicle claims. Roden owns deep ATV (product, rental, road, rollover, child) and golf-cart (DUI, rollover, ejection, pedestrian, vehicle) coverage — gap is UTV/side-by-side-specific terms and golf-cart rental liability.

themes.label: Boating and watercraft
themes.rationale: Coastal markets (Charleston Harbor, Savannah River, Murrells Inlet, Hilton Head approach) generate boat, jet ski, and pontoon-rental claims year-round. Roden owns boating, jet-ski, pontoon, sailboat, speedboat, tugboat, and boating-under-influence pages — gap is rental-defect and wake-related claims.

themes.label: Uninsured / underinsured motorist and coverage disputes
themes.rationale: SC permits UM/UIM stacking (§ 38-77-160); GA generally does not (O.C.G.A. § 33-7-11). Hit-and-run and uninsured-driver claims convert into UM claims, distinct enough to deserve their own ranker — and Roden has no dedicated UIM page despite tracking 'uninsured motorist lawyer'.

themes.rationale: Highest case values. Roden owns brain-injury, spinal-cord, burn, and wrongful-death pillars but they read as generic verticals — narrowing the search query to crash-context ('brain injury car accident lawyer', 'wrongful death truck accident lawyer') better matches MVA-only scope and competitive intent.

keywordScope.label: Motor vehicle, vulnerable road user, and transport-accident verticals only
keywordScope.rule: Limit the keyword universe to vehicle / transport accident verticals only. EVERY keyword in themes, long_tail, gaps, and tracking_set must center on one of these injury vectors: car, truck (incl. commercial / 18-wheeler / box truck / delivery), motorcycle, ride-share (Uber/Lyft), taxi/limo/shuttle, bus, pedestrian, bicycle, e-scooter, e-bike, ATV / side-by-side / off-road vehicle, golf cart, boat / jet ski / personal watercraft. Catastrophic outcomes (brain injury, spinal cord, burn, fatal/wrongful death) and incident-modifier sub-types (DUI, uninsured/underinsured motorist, hit-and-run, rear-end, head-on, multi-vehicle, rollover, T-bone, distracted driving, drowsy driving, lane change, left-turn) are allowed ONLY when paired with an in-scope vertical (e.g. 'wrongful death car accident lawyer', 'brain injury motorcycle crash lawyer'). Do NOT include premises liability, slip-and-fall, dog bite, medical malpractice, nursing home / elder abuse, workers compensation, construction accident, scaffold fall, product liability (unless defective vehicle/restraint/tire), Jones Act / longshore (unless boat collision), or any standalone non-transport vertical. If a competitor covers an out-of-scope vertical, do NOT flag it as a gap. Generic top-of-funnel PI terms ('personal injury lawyer', 'best personal injury lawyer', 'free consultation injury lawyer') are acceptable as broad anchor keywords because Roden's PI practice is constrained to in-scope verticals — keep these to ≤ 3 of the 25-keyword tracking set.
